newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Omega Oil stake in US gas success.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Omega Oil stake in US gas success.

text.p: Oil and gas producer Omega Oil NL said on Tuesday an onshore well in the United States in which it had a five percent interest had encountered a major gas resource.

Omega said in a statement the onshore Fleetwood Trust 1-16 well, operated by Kerr-McGee Corporation in the Texan Anadarko Basin, had struck a major resource in its primary objective, the Puryear formation.
The well had been drilled to a depth of 4,775 metres and logs had been run, it said.
Top of the reservoir was encountered at a depth of 4,620.5 metres and the base at 4,673.9 metres, for a gross thickness of 53.4 metres, it said.
Omega managing director Doug Jenry said it was not possible to accurately estimate potential gas reserves given currently available data.
"However, reserves in comparable wells in the immediate area range from 20-50 billion cubic feet of gas per well, highlighting the potential of this to be a very significant discovery," he said.

Current plans were for casing to be run to total depth and the well to be completed for production testing purposes before year-end, with a view to continuous production commencing during the first quarter of 1997, he said.
Jenry said Omega also had settled its recent acquisition of Discovery Petroleum NL's 24.3 percent interest in the Katnook and Haselgrove gas fields in South Australia's Otway Basin.
"The cashflow from the Katnook and Haselgrove fields will underpin our activities for many years to come and gives us the flexibility to pursue a whole range of opportunities," he said.
